description: kb ambient surfaces. UserPromptSubmit fires kb-pull TWICE, as two SEPARATE hook outputs: --channel=hints (score-floored hints naming what the KB holds about this prompt) and --channel=digest (the rolling session digest). They are split because the platform bounds each hook OUTPUT at ~10 KB, not the event — PROBED 2026-09-14: two hooks on one event delivered ~7 KB each, 14 KB combined, neither stubbed. Sharing one output meant the digest's budget was 'bound minus whatever the hints emitted', so a busy hints turn silently starved the session's own memory. Each channel keeps its OWN home-side state file; they never write the same one. SessionStart (kb-session-start): archive the previous sitting's digest so 'now' stays honest, and cue an unseeded project once. All fail-open; none blocks a tool call. The Stop hook (kb-scribe) is RETIRED as of 0.9.0 — its enforcement ships as the 'session-digest' duty in turn-end, because two plugins each owning a blocking Stop hook re-armed each other.
